What are they demanding? HRTC pensioners protested against the state government over pending demands, including DA arrears. They demanded equal benefits for retired employees and announced plans to gherao the corporation’s headquarters on November 27 Jocelyn Fernandes Updated 16 Nov 2026, 09:26 AM IST Prefer Livemint on Google HRTC pensioners protested against the Himachal Pradesh state government over pending demands, including DA arrears. ( AI-generated image used for representational purpose ) AI Quick Read DA hike, arrears: Pensioners of the Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) are protesting against the state government for fulfilment of a number of pending demands, including hike in dearness allowance and arrears for previous increase, according to an ANI report. In a statement, Dev Raj Thakur, President of the Transport Pensioners Welfare Association, Himachal Pradesh said that the demands are not excessive and pensioners are “merely seeking parity with what the state government has already provided to other pensioners”, it added. “Serving employees have been granted a 3% DA along with their arrears, whereas we were given the 3% DA without any arrears… The government must find a resolution to this,” Thakur explained. He added that the protestors plan to lay siege (gherao) to the corporation’s headquarters on 27 November. Also Read | Bank holiday today: Are Patna, Ranchi branches closed for Chhath Puja on 16 Nov? Why are HRTC pensioners protesting? Earlier on 12 November, HRTC pensioners staged a protest outside the office of the corporation’s Managing Director in Shimla and accused the state of failing to fulfil its assurances made ahead of Diwali , as per the report. They also sought fulfilment of long-pending financial demands. Protesting under the banner of the HRTC Pensioners Welfare Association and the HP Pensioners Joint Action Committee, they have alleged discriminatory treatment of retired employees, particularly regarding DA, pension arrears and other retirement benefits. Brij Lal Thakur, Media in-charge of the HRTC Pensioners JAC in Himachal Pradesh, said pensioners had been struggling to receive their dues for the past four years, but neither the state government nor the corporation management had seriously addressed their concerns. Also Read | FD interest rates hike: See money gains at this bank for ₹1-5 lakh deposits He said pensioners had been protesting despite their advanced age and difficult weather conditions. Their main demand was that HRTC pensioners should receive the same benefits as other state government pensioners. What are demands raised by HRTC pensioners? Thakur said the organisation had 16 demands, with the main being that HRTC pensioners are provided the same benefits as state government pensioners. According to him, pensioners were seeking the following: Implementation of financial orders issued by the Finance Department, including pension revision benefits and additional pension allowances of 5%, 10% and 15% for those aged 65, 70 and 75 years, respectively. “Thousands of cases related to these benefits were still pending, even after pensioners had approached the tribunal, High Court and Supreme Court over nearly 14 years,” he stated. He further alleged that arrears under the Assured Career Progression (ACP) scheme, pending since the tenure of former Chief Minister Virbhadra Singh, had also not been cleared. Also Read | Why India Inc's top bosses are earning 100 times their employees He also questioned the government’s decision to grant only a 3% DA increase to HRTC pensioners, as their demand was for an 8% increase, in line with the benefits sought by other state pensioners. He added that the government has also failed to clear pending arrears , claiming that the outstanding dues amounted to hundreds of crores of rupees. Referring to the recent High Court directions on the payment of pension-related arrears, Thakur welcomed the decision and urged the government to release the first instalment by December 15 and the second by February 28, 2027, along with interest. Pensioners to intensify protests? He warned that pensioners would intensify their agitation and gherao legislators, ministers, Deputy Chief Minister and Chief Minister if their demands remained unresolved. He also threatened protests in Haroli, the constituency of Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri, and Nadaun, represented by Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. Also Read | Delhi AQI 800: Capital ‘breathes poison’, ranks world’s 6th most polluted city Thakur said HRTC had approximately 8,700 pensioners and around 12,000 serving employees, adding that of these, nearly 11,000 retired employees and around 8,500 pensioners were associated with the organisation. He warned that the agitation would be intensified if the government failed to respond to their demands. Pensioners from across Himachal Pradesh would gather in Shimla on 27 November, with their families to continue the agitation and gherao the HRTC headquarters, he added. The protest on Friday was part of a wider agitation being organised by pensioners across the state over their pending financial and retirement-related demands.
